paragraphs: Children in care from Bromley live with carers approved by the council's own fostering service or by the independent agencies shown above. The council says it has a diverse group of children who need foster care, and that it always aims to place its own children with its own carers first. For someone weighing the council against an agency, that is the practical difference Bromley points to: its carers are likely to have more regular local placements, with children in local schools and contact meetings held in the borough. Agencies recruit across wider areas and set their own pay and support, so ask each one how often it places children from Bromley.

You can apply to Bromley if you are over 21, single, living with a partner or married, and own or rent a home with a spare bedroom for a foster child. You need to keep a smoke-free home for the child even if you smoke, and short-term carers need to live within an hour of the borough. No qualifications are needed, but some experience of having children around you is. The council asks for two personal references, a medical report and enhanced DBS checks for every adult in the household, runs a preparation group over three separate days, and holds six to eight assessment interviews. It aims to finish the whole assessment within 16 weeks, after which its fostering panel makes a recommendation.

Once approved, Bromley carers have a supervising social worker, a 24-hour out-of-hours duty team with extra fostering support on weekday evenings and weekends, THRIVE therapeutic support, membership of the Fostering Network and the Bromley Foster Care Association, and fostering hubs of six to eight families who meet to support each other. Carers who transfer from another service, and households who recommend a friend who is then approved, receive £1,000 in vouchers.

Bromley sets out its weekly allowances and carer's fees, with extra payments at Christmas, for birthdays and for the summer holidays, on its own rates page. That page does not say which year the figures are for, so ask the fostering team for the current rates.

Speak to the council and to two or three of the services above before you decide. If you live near the borough's edge, see our pages for Croydon, Lewisham, Greenwich and Bexley, or South London and London as a whole.
